pr_body:
Closes #98354.

This PR introduces a cache of MsQuicConfiguration objects which configure few aspect of MsQuic connections:
- ALPN protocols
- Certificate to be used
- Client vs Server connection
- Requiring client auth, configuring cipher suite, ...

The most critical is the certificate. On Linux, MsQuic uses statically linked OpenSSL fork, so the certificate is specified by serializing it to a buffer in PKCS12 format and deserializing it on the MsQuic side. Caching the configuration objects allows us to do this serialization once per app lifetime instead of doing it again for each connection and it will gives us a basis for features like TLS Resumption.

issue_context.title: [QUIC] Implement MsQuicConfiguration cache
issue_context.body:
On linux, creating the `MsQuicConfiguration` object is expensive because we need to export the X509Certificate in PKCS12 format. Doing this for each connection separately is a waste of resources. MsQuicConfiguration objects are designed to be shared between connections. We should look into implementing a configuration cache similar to what we have for SslStream on Windows.

Preliminary benchmarks suggest this should significantly reduce handshake time and thus time-to-first-byte and related metrics in HTTP/3.

Implementing a cache for the MsQuicConfiguration objects will allow us to also later implement TLS Session resumption, allowing even faster handshake.

review_comments: Curious, why do we need an escape hatch for this one?

Although I have tried to stress the cache to hammer out the possible weird concurrency bugs (and did not find any in the last version), I prefer to have an option to disable it in case a customer hits an issue.

Why can't this be part of the following loop? Why the new handle has to be treated separately? I.e. this line:
```suggestion
```
and line 172:
```
while (cached != handle && !cached.TryAddRentCount());
-->
while (!cached.TryAddRentCount());
```

There is an opportunity for live-lock in the suggested version:

- we add the `handle` in the cache
- parallel cleanup of the cache closes the handle
- this thread tries to `TryAddRentCount()`, but it fails and will attempt to add the (closed) handle again and will spin forever as the `TryAddRentCount` never succeeds
